images.title: Many rides, one number
images.purpose: Show that the statement about 15 minutes sums up many ride times that vary, which is what makes it a statistical statement.
images.composition: One dot plot sits in the lower middle of the frame; an arrow from the dots points up to one short summary label, with wide white space.
exact_structure: A horizontal grey (#6B7280) number line from 12 to 18 with a tick at every whole number and each tick numbered: 12, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17, 18.
Exactly 5 teal (#0072B2) dots, one above each of 13, 14, 15, 16 and 17; no dots at 12 or 18.
The caption Ride home (minutes) under the number line.
A curved bracket in grey over the 5 dots, with an arrow rising from its centre to a reddish purple (#CC79A7) rounded label reading about 15 minutes, placed above the 15 tick.
Arithmetic check for the reviewer only, NOT drawn in the frame: (13 + 14 + 15 + 16 + 17) ÷ 5 = 75 ÷ 5 = 15.
rejection: a dot at 12 or 18, or two dots stacked on one value
the summary label showing any number other than 15
images.takeaway: A statistical statement sums up many varying observations in one number.
images.description: A dot plot of five ride times at 13, 14, 15, 16 and 17 minutes, with an arrow to the label about 15 minutes.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video for this concept.
images.teaching_notes: Point to the spread of dots first, then to the word about, which tells us the data varies.

image_decisions.why: A small dot plot shows the varying data hidden behind one statistical statement.
